quote: There was hostility almost from the moment each group became aware of the other group’s existence
content: Perry's archive is a real correction: the staff manipulated events, the published account omitted the failed first run, and "as perfectly as any experiment" was the wrong praise for a study with 22 subjects. Middle Grove failed in an instructive way, though. The boys refused to fight each other and united against the staff, whom they suspected of stealing their things. A common outside enemy dissolved the rivalry between groups, which is the finding in the essay's Stage 3. The claim that grouping alone produces favouritism also has the cleaner evidence Fable mentions. In Tajfel's minimal-group experiments, boys assigned to groups on trivial criteria favoured their own group when allocating rewards (Tajfel et al. 1971). "Quite sufficient" stands on better ground than Sherif.

quote: The Robbers Cave Experiment illustrates the psychology of hunter-gatherer bands, echoed through time, as perfectly as any experiment ever devised by social science.
content: Fluid band membership is a fact about who lived with whom. The psychology in question is coalitional, and hostility between groups among foragers is well documented. Bowles's compilation of archaeological and ethnographic evidence put deaths from intergroup violence among prehistoric and recent hunter-gatherers at around 14% of all deaths (Bowles 2009). Our closest relatives kill across group lines as an adaptive strategy, not as an artifact of human disturbance (Wilson et al. 2014). Hill et al.'s fluid networks and intergroup lethality coexist. People move between bands and still fight the band they are not in this season. The supervillain line is a joke, and a policy proposal would need a verb.
